english_meaning: A mound or ridge of sand formed by wind, especially in deserts or near coasts.
gujarati_meaning: પવન વડે ઢેરો થઈ ગયેલ રેતીનો ઢૂવો — રણ કે દરિયા-કિનારે.
usage_note: Dunes constantly shift shape due to wind; some reach 100+ metres high.
memory_tip: 'Dune' → 'D' = desert → desert + mound = sand dune = રેતીનો ઢૂવો.
examples: The Thar Desert is famous for its vast sand dunes.
Tourists ride camels across the golden dunes.
Coastal dunes protect shorelines from erosion.
The dunes shifted overnight due to strong winds.

english_meaning: A tree or shrub that grows in coastal saline or brackish water in tropical regions.
gujarati_meaning: ઉષ્ણ-દરિયા-કિનારા પર ખારા અથવા ઓછા ખારા પાણીમાં ઉગ્યો — ઊભા મૂળ ધરાવ — ચેર-ઝાડ.
usage_note: Mangroves protect coastlines from erosion and storms, and support rich biodiversity.
memory_tip: 'Man' + 'grove' → a grove for the sea-man → દરિયા-કિનારા પર ઝૂ.
examples: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest.
Mangroves act as natural barriers against cyclones.
Many fish species breed in mangrove swamps.
Gujarat's coastal mangroves are being restored by NGOs.

english_meaning: A forest dominated by trees that shed their leaves annually during autumn or dry season.
gujarati_meaning: ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર — ઉનાળે અથવા પાનખરે — બધા ઝાડ પાન ખેરવે — તેવો જંગલ.
usage_note: Tropical deciduous forests cover large parts of central India.
memory_tip: 'Deciduous' = ઝાડ (trees) decided to drop leaves = ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર પાન ખેરવ.
examples: India's deciduous forests burst into colour after the monsoon.
Teak and sal trees dominate deciduous forests in India.
Wildlife sanctuaries are often set in deciduous forests.
The deciduous forest floor is rich in leaf litter.

english_meaning: The transfer of pollen from one flower to another, enabling plant fertilization.
gujarati_meaning: એક ફૂલથી બીજા ફૂલ પર પરાગ-ટ્રાન્સફર — ફળ-ઉત્પત્તિ શક્ય બને.
usage_note: Bees are the most important pollinators; without them food production collapses.
examples: Bees play a crucial role in the pollination of crops.
Without pollination, many plants cannot produce fruit.
Pollination can occur via wind, insects, or birds.
Declining bee populations threaten pollination worldwide.

english_meaning: The process by which green plants use sunlight to synthesize food from carbon dioxide and water.
gujarati_meaning: લીલા છોડ સૂર્ય-પ્રકાશ, CO₂ અને પાણી વડે ખોરાક ઉત્પન્ન કરે — ઓક્સિજન ઉત્સર્જ.
usage_note: Produces oxygen as a by-product — essential for all aerobic life.
examples: Photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy.
Without photosynthesis, there would be no oxygen on Earth.
The rate of photosynthesis increases with more light.
Scientists are studying artificial photosynthesis for clean energy.

english_meaning: To spend the winter in a dormant state, with greatly reduced metabolic activity.
gujarati_meaning: શિયાળો ઊંઘ-અવસ્થામાં — ઘણા ઓછા ચયાપચય સાથે — વિતાવવો.
usage_note: Bears, hedgehogs, and some bats hibernate; they live off stored fat.
examples: Bears hibernate from November through March.
Some snakes hibernate in rocky dens during winter.
Hibernating animals reduce their heart rate dramatically.
Scientists study hibernation for insights into human medicine.

english_meaning: The use of colours or patterns to blend into the natural environment and avoid detection.
gujarati_meaning: આ-પ-પ-ઉ (surroundings) સ-ઉ (with) ભ-ળ-ઉ (blend) — દ-ઉ (enemy) ન-ઉ (cannot see) — camouflage = છૂ-પ-ઉ (hide).
usage_note: Many animals use camouflage to hunt or avoid predators.
examples: The chameleon is famous for its natural camouflage.
Arctic foxes turn white in winter as camouflage against snow.
Leaf insects have evolved perfect camouflage.
Camouflage patterns are used in military uniforms.

english_meaning: The seasonal movement of animals from one region to another, typically for feeding or breeding.
gujarati_meaning: ઋતુ-ક્રમ અનુસાર પ્રાણી/પક્ષી ખોરાક અથવા પ્રજ-ઉ-ઉ (breeding) માટે દૂ-ર (far) પ્રવ-ઉ-ઉ (journey).
usage_note: The wildebeest migration in Africa and bird migration to India are iconic examples.
memory_tip: 'Migrate' = move across → migration = ઋ-ઉ-ઉ (seasonal) moving = પ-ઉ-ઉ (journey).
examples: Flamingos migrate to Gujarat's Rann of Kutch in winter.
The wildebeest migration is called the Great Migration.
Climate change is altering bird migration patterns.
Millions of butterflies migrate to Mexico every autumn.

english_meaning: An animal that hunts, kills, and eats other animals.
gujarati_meaning: બ-ઉ-ઉ (other) પ-ઉ-ઉ (animals) ખ-ઉ (eat) — ઉ (hunt and kill for food) — predator = ઉ-ઉ (hunter).
usage_note: Apex predators like tigers and lions are at the top of the food chain.
examples: The tiger is an apex predator in Indian forests.
Predators control the population of prey animals.
The loss of predators disrupts the ecological balance.
Wolves are being reintroduced to control deer populations.

english_meaning: A complex network of living organisms and their physical environment interacting together.
gujarati_meaning: સ-ઉ-ઉ (all organisms) + ઉ-ઉ-ઉ (environment) = એ-ઉ (a network of life) — ecosystem = જ-ઉ-ઉ-ઉ (life-network).
usage_note: Disrupting one part of an ecosystem affects all other parts.
examples: The Amazon rainforest is the world's most biodiverse ecosystem.
Coral reefs are among the most productive ecosystems on Earth.
Human activity is destroying natural ecosystems rapidly.
Restoring ecosystems can help combat climate change.

english_meaning: The leaves of a plant or tree collectively.
gujarati_meaning: ઝ-ઉ (tree)/છ-ઉ (plant) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ (all) પ-ઉ (leaves) — collectively — foliage = ઉ-ઉ (leafage).
usage_note: 'Foliage' is used in a formal or botanical context; 'leaves' is more everyday.
memory_tip: 'Folio' = leaf/page → foliage = many leaves = ઝ-ઉ ન-ઉ (tree's) leaves.
examples: The autumn foliage of New England attracts many tourists.
Dense foliage kept the forest floor cool.
The foliage of the tropical tree provides habitat for birds.
Heavy rain knocked the foliage from the trees.

english_meaning: A group of living organisms able to interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (organisms) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ-ઉ (same kind) — that can breed together — species = ઉ-ઉ (type/kind).
usage_note: There are an estimated 8.7 million species on Earth, most still undiscovered.
memory_tip: 'Species' → 'spec' = special kind → species = special type of life.
examples: The Bengal tiger is an endangered species.
Scientists discovered a new species of frog in the Amazon.
Protecting species diversity is vital for ecosystem health.
India hosts over 500 species of migratory birds.

english_meaning: The uppermost layer of a forest formed by the crowns of the tallest trees.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (forest) ન-ઉ (of) ઉ-ઉ (tallest trees) ઉ-ઉ (crowns) — roof-like top layer — canopy = ઉ-ઉ (tree-roof).
usage_note: The canopy intercepts most sunlight; organisms below are adapted to shade.
examples: The rainforest canopy is home to monkeys and toucans.
Little sunlight penetrates the dense canopy to the forest floor.
Scientists study canopy life using elevated walkways.
The canopy acts as a shield against heavy rain.

english_meaning: The variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat or on Earth.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (all) પ-ઉ/ઉ-ઉ (plants/animals) ઉ-ઉ (variety) — bio-diversity = ઉ-ઉ (life variety).
usage_note: India is one of the 17 megadiverse countries in the world.
examples: The Amazon rainforest has unparalleled biodiversity.
India is a megadiverse country with rich biodiversity.
Biodiversity loss threatens food security and medicine.
Protected areas are essential for preserving biodiversity.

english_meaning: Active at night rather than during the day.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (night) ઉ-ઉ (active) — that which is active at night — nocturnal = ઉ-ઉ (night-active).
usage_note: Owls, bats, and leopards are examples of nocturnal animals.
examples: Owls are nocturnal hunters with excellent night vision.
The leopard is a nocturnal predator.
Many desert animals are nocturnal to avoid daytime heat.
Scientists use infrared cameras to study nocturnal wildlife.

english_meaning: A close, long-term interaction between two different species, often mutually beneficial.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (two) ઉ-ઉ (different) ઉ-ઉ (species) ઉ-ઉ (close) ઉ-ઉ (relationship) — often both benefit — symbiosis.
usage_note: Bees and flowers, clownfish and sea anemones are classic examples.
examples: The relationship between bees and flowers is a form of symbiosis.
Clownfish and sea anemones have a symbiotic relationship.
Fungi and tree roots form symbiosis called mycorrhizae.
Symbiosis allows both organisms to thrive in harsh environments.

english_meaning: A plant with thick, fleshy leaves or stems that store water, adapted to arid conditions.
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (water) ઉ-ઉ (store) — ઉ-ઉ (thick leaves/stems) — dry climate adaptable plant — succulent.
usage_note: Cacti are the most well-known succulents; aloe vera is a widely used succulent.
memory_tip: 'Succulent' = juicy (succulent food) → plant that's 'juicy' inside = stores water.
examples: Aloe vera is a widely used succulent with medicinal properties.
Succulents are popular houseplants because they need little water.
Desert succulents survive months without rainfall.
The cactus is the most iconic succulent of the Sonoran Desert.

english_meaning: The ecological interaction where one organism (predator) hunts and feeds on another (prey).
gujarati_meaning: ઉ-ઉ (predator) ઉ-ઉ (hunts) ઉ-ઉ (prey) — ઉ-ઉ (ecological) ઉ-ઉ (balance) — predator-prey relationship.
usage_note: Loss of predators leads to prey overpopulation and ecosystem imbalance.
memory_tip: Predator = hunter; prey = hunted → predator-prey = hunter-hunted relationship.
examples: The wolf-deer predator-prey relationship keeps forest ecosystems balanced.
Studying predator-prey relationships helps in wildlife conservation.
A disrupted predator-prey dynamic can collapse entire ecosystems.
The cheetah-gazelle predator-prey relationship is studied globally.
